02.alt: The sign-in page, with the Sign in with passkey button and the Recover your account link
02.caption: The sign-in page. Your first sign-in on a device creates your account.
02.heading: Sign in with a passkey

02.alt: The onboarding page at 1 of 5 steps complete: the passkey step is done and the name, affiliation and email fields are empty
02.caption: Onboarding after the first sign-in. The passkey step is already done.
02.heading: Set up your account (onboarding)

02.alt: A recovery request with 3 of 3 guardian approvals, the Check for approvals button and the open 72-hour safety window
02.caption: Three guardians have approved. The new passkey takes over when the 72-hour safety window ends.
02.heading: Recover a lost account

02.alt: The Security page with the Devices card, five recovery guardians and the Change guardians button, Recovery requests and Key rotation
02.caption: The Security page lists this device's key, your five guardians and any recovery requests waiting for you.
02.heading: Security settings

03.alt: The paper list on the Following tab, with two papers, each showing authors, category, version, age, abstract and an Under review chip
03.caption: The Following tab shows new papers in the categories you follow.
03.heading: The paper list

03.alt: Keyword search results for "calibration", with the Keyword and Semantic toggle, Save this search, and the category, date and status filters
03.caption: A keyword search. The filters on the left count the matches in each category and status.
03.heading: Search

03.alt: A paper page: title, authors, Under review chip, PDF, HTML, Cite, Download and Report, with the margin open on the Reviews tab
03.caption: A paper page. The margin beside the text holds the verification badge, the paper ID and six tabs.
03.heading: The paper page

03.alt: A paper page with a Corrected banner above the title that gives the authors' reason and a View record link
03.caption: A correction notice puts a banner above the title of every version.
03.heading: Banners

04.alt: The Proof tab: signed by all 3 listed authors, version history intact, files match, recorded in the public log, timestamp anchor pending, no retraction or correction, preserved in 1 of 1 local copy
04.caption: The Proof tab lists each check your browser ran. Anchor pending is expected in this release.
04.heading: The Proof tab

04.alt: The Verify a file page after a PDF was dropped, showing This file matches what the authors signed and naming the paper and version
04.caption: The file matches a signed version. Only its fingerprint left your device.
04.heading: Check a file you already have

04.alt: The Download menu open on a paper page, offering the Paper archive with the scholium verify command for it
04.caption: Download, then Paper archive, saves the .car file that the command-line verifier checks.
04.heading: Check offline with the command-line verifier

04.alt: The Network page with the This node, Log head, Public timestamp (Anchor pending) and Probe pass rate cards
04.caption: The network page shows who runs the server, the head of its public log and its timestamp status.
04.heading: The network page

05.alt: The Files step with the Paper and Code and data drop zones, and main.pdf uploaded with the role Paper PDF and its fingerprint matched
05.caption: Step 1. Each uploaded file gets a role and is fingerprinted on your device.
05.heading: Step 1: Files

05.alt: The Authors step with the Add a co-author form and two authors, each with CRediT roles selected and move up and down buttons
05.caption: Step 3. Add co-authors by DID and give everyone at least one CRediT role.
05.heading: Step 3: Authors

05.alt: The status tracker: Submitted done, Co-author consents 0 of 2 in progress with a Sign your consent button, then Scan, Moderation, Listed and AI pre-review not started
05.caption: The tracker after submitting. The version waits until every author, including you, signs a consent.
05.heading: After you submit: the status tracker

05.alt: The Issue a notice dialog with Correction selected over Retraction and Withdrawal, and a reason filled in
05.caption: Issue notice offers a correction, a retraction or a withdrawal. A reason is required.
05.heading: Corrections, retractions and withdrawals

06.alt: The review form beside the paper: a You are reviewing anonymously notice, a conflict check with all three checks passed, and a sealed review of v1
06.caption: The review form runs the conflict check and states whether you review anonymously.
06.heading: 2. The conflict check

06.alt: The Reviews page with Reviewer A revealed, recommending Minor revisions with six scores and justifications, and Reviewer B not yet revealed
06.caption: A revealed review shows its rubric and recommendation. A sealed one shows nothing yet.
06.heading: 6. Reveal the review

07.alt: A paper's Discussion tab with no posts yet and a Sign in to start a thread or reply prompt
07.caption: Anyone can read a discussion. Posting needs a signed-in member.
07.heading: Who can take part

08.alt: The AI pre-review page with the Advisory banner and a Methodology finding showing severity, confidence, a quotation from the paper and Rebut, Confirm and Wrong buttons
08.caption: Each finding names its severity, confidence and evidence. The banner marks the report as advisory.
08.heading: How to read a finding

09.alt: The moderation decision page with the paper on the left and, on the right, policy clause MOD-03, the reason for the author and the preview of what the author will see
09.caption: A decision names a policy clause and a reason. The preview shows what the author will read.
09.heading: For moderators: the console

09.alt: The Appeal the moderation decision dialog over a paper held from listing, showing the moderator's reason and the author's grounds for appeal
09.caption: The appeal form quotes the moderator's reason. Your grounds are required.
09.heading: Appeals

09.alt: An appeal waiting for the panel, with the decision appealed, the grounds, and the panel vote form with Outcome and Your reasons
09.caption: A panel member reads the decision and the grounds, then votes with a reason.
09.heading: If you are on a panel

09.alt: The Report this paper dialog with reasons from Research misconduct to Something else, and Duplicated figures selected
09.caption: Reporting a paper. A moderator reviews every report and tells you the outcome.
09.heading: Reporting content
